rationale:
Decision: resubmit the verified best design exactly as it raced in iteration 7 and iteration 8 (score 344.4979). The round-2 critique and the authorized entity1 text describe a different configuration (kd 0.25, line_loss 'search_left'). I reject that configuration as the submission because the outcome record does not support it. Iteration 7's design, as recorded in the outcome table and produced in my own history, was kd 0.35, ki 0.5, kp 2.0, base_speed 1.5, line_loss 'last_direction'. That is the only configuration with a measured score of 344.4979, and iteration 8 reproduced it to four decimals on all 60 trials. The search_left and kd 0.25 variant has never raced, so it has no evidence behind it.

What I kept: every value of the raced 344.5 design, including geometry (five 12 mm sensors at x = -0.02 to +0.02 m, y = 0.05 m; body 0.18 x 0.12 m; mass 0.8 kg; wheel_track 0.12 m; wheel_radius 0.03 m) and the controller (kp 2.0, ki 0.5, kd 0.35, base_speed 1.5, line_loss 'last_direction', weights -2 to 2).

What I did not change: no new single-variable test. Critique points against kd 0.4 and against search_left are accepted as reasons not to advance them now. Points that the final track may differ from the oval are noted, but the s-bend and slalom failures have no tested fix that would not risk the only proven gain.

Expected result: about 344.5 on the development set, with oval completion near 0.85 (17 of 20), and s-bend and slalom still failing (progress about 0.34 and 0.11). Reproducibility is already shown by iteration 8, so this race is a repeat check and adds little new information. The next iteration, if any single-variable test is run, should state its baseline as kd 0.35 / last_direction.
